  • Sep 24, 2026CorrectionMission Bay

    Removed a mistagged 'planned' status from a 2032 milestone that would revert this complete, open school on the timeline. View record →

    Full text

    An audit for other records with the same bug reported on 'Prequel Park (Power Station sub-area)' found this record's 2032-08 milestone ("School is planned to grow one grade per year into a full TK-5 (with Preschool) campus") carried status: 'planned', even though the school is already built and open (live status: complete). The site's timeline renderer treats any dated status-setting milestone as the record's status as of that date, so scrubbing the timeline past August 2032 would have shown this already-open school reverting to 'planned' (pre-construction). The milestone describes enrollment growth, not a change in construction status, so it should never have carried a status field at all -- removed it. The milestone's date, text and sources are unchanged.

  • Sep 23, 2026CoverageAll sites

    Split Chase Center's shared parcel from Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4; merged Harmonic Brewing's building in.

    Full text

    The owner identified that DataSF's Assessor Parcel dataset gives Chase Center (formerly tracked as status.csv blklot 8722025) and the neighboring Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 office towers (formerly blklot 8722063) byte-identical geometry -- one shared master-condominium-association land parcel spanning the whole Mission Bay South Blocks 29-32 superblock (confirmed: Chase Center, both Uber towers, a parking structure and a small broadcast building are all separate condo units on one shared plat). This made the two records' polygons fully overlapping on the map -- a click anywhere in the shared area could resolve to either record, and each record's own "Where it is" mini-map showed the wrong footprint. Migrated both records off status.csv onto hand-derived, non-overlapping real geometry: Chase Center (record_id mission_bay_chase_center) is now the full Assessor parcel with both Uber towers' own real OpenStreetMap building footprints subtracted out; Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 (record_id mission_bay_uber_3_4) is now the union of those same two real OSM footprints. The owner also identified that Harmonic Brewing's own standalone taproom building, at the NE edge of the site (7 Warriors Way Ste 206 per its DataSF business-registration address; the registry's geocode puts Harmonic Brewing, Miller & Lux and Cupcakin' at the same point, so it does not place any of them in a particular building), and Miller & Lux (7 Warriors Way Ste 208 per its registration address; its position inside the arena footprint is not established by the registry) are both Chase Center/Thrive City tenants, not separate structures -- Harmonic Brewing's building is included in Chase Center's new geometry (it falls within the parcel-minus-Uber-towers remainder) rather than tracked as a separate record. Re-running the retail spatial join (src/join_retail.py) against the corrected geometry surfaced three more Thrive City business registrations -- Cupcakin' Bake Shop (Ste 200), 'Siren SF' (1 Warriors Way Unit 24, shown as Siren Cafe & Bar) and The Sarap Shop (1 Warriors Way) -- registrations at Chase Center addresses, not proof of open storefronts; see those rows; see those changelog rows.

    docs/briefs/mission-bay-geometry.md

    Full text

    Verified a second research batch covering the 16 records this project had deliberately left undated (docs/briefs/research-verification-2.md). Confirmed and added: Mission Bay Block 34 gained a May 2020 UC Regents preliminary-plans item and its August 2024 completion date firmed to the exact day (Aug 27), while a claimed April 2021 garage-construction-start date was checked and rejected -- a Commercial Property Executive article directly contradicts it, showing the garage broke ground after, not before, the clinical building. Park P10 gained two real earlier-stage milestones from a directly-read EPA/DTSC brownfields fact sheet that names "Mission Bay Park P10" specifically, and a 2011 press-tour article -- while a companion Board of Supervisors citation given for a different record (P11/P11A) turned out, on direct Legistar lookup, to reference an unrelated Graffiti Advisory Board appointment and was rejected outright. Avalon at Mission Bay II gained a real Q1 2005 construction-start date from the developer's own SEC-filed earnings release. 255 Berry's existing 2004 completion milestone had its source upgraded from a generic listing search to the developer's own project page. Mission Creek Park (the P3 extension) gained an October 2022 completion date from a Landscape Performance Series case study, closing a gap this record's own open_questions had already flagged (whether a fall-2021 target opening actually happened -- it slipped a year further). Two records (the P26 interchange wedge and Block 22) had the claimed dates confirmed as flat misattributions -- the cited Port Commission/Lotus Water material is entirely about the already-tracked Bayfront Park (P22), not either record -- so nothing was added to either. Five more records (The Beacon, Mission Bay Commons, the Creek Park's own P1-P3 segment as distinct from P3, and the three UCSF garage/utility-plant records) returned no independently confirmable date after this pass and were left as-is, several due to realestate.ucsf.edu's persistent block on automated access. Superseded the same day: Clark Construction's own press release states the garage portion started in April 2021, so the April 2021 date rejected above was restored by the third research batch (see the 2026-09-22 row of that name). Accuracy audit 2026-09 (2026-09-29) note: the outcomes listed here for P11/P11A, Avalon II, 255 Berry, Mission Creek Park P3 and P26/Block 22 come from Legistar, SEC and Landscape Performance Series pages that were not re-read in the audit, and the May 2020 Regents item and Aug 27 2024 completion for Block 34 could not be read (realestate.ucsf.edu, stantec.com and commercialsearch.com return 403).

Citations were real and quotable far more often this time, but two of the 13 claims were still rejected before verification even started -- both cited real documents describing a different physical parcel than this project tracks (Block 22 vs. Bayfront Park/P22, confirmed ~500m apart and matching UCSF's own "Koret Quad" label; the P26 interchange wedge vs. the real, separately-named Mariposa Park, confirmed via San Francisco's own Legistar API that the cited ordinance's own title places it on a different street). Of the remaining 11: confirmed and added -- Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 gained two 2018 structural-steel milestones (Mortenson's own steel-fabrication page, distinct from the arena's steel package) and a JV-formation note (Alexandria Real Estate's own SEC filing); Mission Bay Commons gained a narrower, accurately-worded Nov 2011 completion milestone for Park P16 specifically (the source names only P16, not P17, and says "recently completed," not "dedicated," as the fuller claim implied); Mission Bay Block 34 gained a real April 2021 garage-construction-start date from Clark Construction's own press release, reversing this project's own prior rejection of the same date (which had relied on a vaguer secondary paraphrase). Caught and rejected: P11/P11A's claimed Board of Supervisors File #190755 was re-checked directly against Legistar's API and confirmed, again, not to exist; UCSF's 1670 Owens Garage citation turned out to be about a different, separately-addressed UCSF garage (1625 Owens St, serving the Rutter Center) three streets away. Flagged, not resolved: a real identity question about whether mission_bay_creek_park_p1_p3 actually belongs to Mission Bay North's own NP1/NP2 open-space system rather than the Mission Bay South labels it currently carries. Left as-is: the UCSF Preliminary Utilities Plant and part of the Third Street Garage's own completion date, both blocked by realestate.ucsf.edu's persistent 403 (tried direct fetch, a reader-proxy, spoofed-user-agent curl, and the Wayback Machine -- the Wayback Machine itself is blocked at this environment's network level). The Third Street Garage did gain a general-contractor fact (Overaa Construction) confirming its identity and and giving 882 parking stalls (the contractor's own project page); an 822-space figure from a 2003 pre-construction budget item was cited but not found in the audit, so the discrepancy is unconfirmed. Accuracy audit 2026-09 (2026-09-29) note: of the Block 22 / Mariposa Park, File #190755, 1670 Owens / 1625 Owens, Mortenson and Alexandria SEC findings above, only 'Koret Quad' as a real UCSF name was confirmed in the audit (Architectural Record, UC Regents Mar 2016); the rest were not re-read.

    Full text

    SECOND correction pass on Mission Bay coverage claims, this time using a proper method: rather than eyeballing footprints, polygonized real city blocks from real street geometry (src/block_fit.py's load_blocks(), the same tool used elsewhere in this project to fit new features against real blocks) and computed, for every real block touching the Mission Bay boundary, what fraction of its actual building footprint area is covered by a tracked record. Of 58 real blocks with >=30% of their area inside the boundary, 33 have meaningful real building coverage (>3% of block area built); this audit found 9 of those 33 were under 50% tracked. Investigated all 9: fixed a real bug in 500 Terry A. Francois Boulevard's own geometry (mission_bay_500_terry_francois.geojson) -- it had only ever captured 1 of 3 real DataSF footprint pieces sharing its mblr (the smallest, ~1172 sq m, missing ~7460 sq m of the real ~8636 sq m building), now corrected to the union of all 3; added 1401 Third Street (an office building, built 2009, about 222,000 sq ft, both per the Assessor roll; tenant not identified) and the Chase Center Parking Garage (150 Warriors Way, built 2009; 469,726 sq ft per a Redfin listing, not a primary source) as new real records. Four blocks remain under 50% tracked: all are minor (building footprint under 17% of their block's area) with no address found in DataSF Assessor parcel data to identify them -- left undocumented rather than guessed, same treatment as the already-investigated 'Community Center Garage' fragment near the Rutter Community Center. This audit method (real polygonized blocks + building-footprint coverage fraction) is more rigorous than the ad hoc satellite spot-checks and footprint-distance scans used in the prior two passes and should be the standard going forward for any future Mission Bay completeness claim.

One map crop for NP4 used a mis-anchored transform that put the wrong area on screen; the owner caught it and it was redone with a proper 2-point similarity transform (Edgewater + the Channel Pump Station, both already-confirmed real positions) before re-confirming.

    Mission Rock map: swapped a thin street highlight for the real street corridor after the owner flagged possible sidewalk overlap.

    Full text

    Mission Rock labeled map: replaced the thin real-street centerline highlight with the real street CORRIDOR (the same curb+centerline buffer join_approximate.py clips against), after the owner flagged Blocks D1/D2/H as appearing to eat the Mission Rock Street sidewalk on sign-off. Measured directly against DataSF's real curb and centerline data: the blocks' south edge (the recorded Assessor lot line) sits ~9.5-10.3m from the street centerline, real curb ~7.2-7.8m -- a genuine ~2.7-3.5m sidewalk gap the blocks already stop short of. No geometry changed; only the map's street rendering, which previously implied a much narrower street than the real right-of-way. Accuracy audit 2026-09 (2026-09-29) note: a quick re-measure against DataSF's curb data did not reproduce the ~7.2-7.8 m curb and ~2.7-3.5 m gap figures (nearest-curb distances from the centerline ran 4.6-7.4 m opposite D1/D2 and 7 m or more opposite H, mixed with crossing curbs), and the source cited here has no URL; treat those figures as approximate and unconfirmed.

    DataSF Street Centerline and Curbs and Islands
  • Sep 18, 2026CorrectionAll sites

    Mission Rock map, round 2: fixed a false pinch in the rendered street edge near Block H caused by a partial curb segment.

    Full text

    Mission Rock labeled map, round 2: the round-1 street-corridor fix above unioned in a real DataSF curb LineString that turns out to cover only part of Block H's Mission Rock St frontage, pulling the rendered street edge in tight under part of H (~1.2m gap) while the rest of the D1/D2/H frontage kept the generic ~3.9-4.3m gap -- a false pinch/step the owner flagged as looking wrong ('should be a straight line'). Checked the block geometry first rather than assume it was wrong: D1, D2 and H's south edges are collinear to within millimeters from their own committed coordinates, and the pure centerline buffer (no curb) already runs as one continuous straight band the full frontage length at the same bearing. Added an include_curbs flag to street_geometry.build_street_buffer() (default True, unchanged for every clipping/QA caller) and set it False only for this one map's rendering, so a partial curb segment can't make an already-straight real street look broken on the one map built to show it plainly. No geometry or clipping logic changed. Accuracy audit 2026-09 (2026-09-29) note: the partial-coverage curb LineString was described from the map work and no DataSF feature id or URL was recorded, so it can't be re-checked from this row; the effect is rendering only.

    DataSF Street Centerline; DataSF Curbs and Islands (partial coverage identified by isolating the one LineString near Block H)

  • Jun 2025RetailPier 70

    Standard Deviant Brewing is a confirmed Building 12 tenant. View record →

    Full text

    The owner flagged that Standard Deviant Brewing, open at 1070 Maryland St (Building 12) since June 2025, was missing. Confirmed via press coverage; it never surfaced in the DataSF registration join at all (checked out/retail_candidates.csv and the raw business-locations pull directly) because it has no Registered Business Location record under any name at that address as of the 2026-09-22 data pull -- a real gap in DataSF's own dataset, not a join bug like the earlier approximate-geometry drops. The automated scan can only be as exhaustive as that source; it will keep missing open, press-covered tenants that haven't filed a registration yet, so periodic manual/press checks stay necessary alongside it. The SF Chronicle (June 4, 2025) announced the taproom would open on Friday, June 6; the SF Standard (June 25, 2025) reported it 'less than two weeks in', so the exact opening day is not confirmed and this row now dates it to June 2025.

    https://sfstandard.com/2025/06/25/standard-deviant-brewing-pier-70-mission-kolsch/ (added Sep 23, 2026)

    Genentech Hall: UC Regents approve an amended $222.4 million capital-improvement budget, funding plan, environmental documentation and design for the 'UC Hall Seismic Replacement, Mission Bay' project (Building 24) -- believed to be this building based on matching gross square footage (433,828 gsf) and programs (structural/chemical biology, molecular/cell/developmental biology), per a January 2000 Regents item recounting the March 1999 action; site preparation began October 1999 and steel-frame construction began December 1999, per the same January 2000 item

    The Regents of the University of California, 2000-01
  • Nov 1998MilestoneMission Bay

    Mission Bay School: The Board of Supervisors adopts the Mission Bay Redevelopment Plan; a neighborhood elementary school was part of its original vision

    The San Francisco Standard, 2026-08-06; Hoodline, 2025-10
  • ~1997MilestonePier 70

    Crane Cove Park: Park first envisioned in the Port's Waterfront Land Use Plan; later carried in the 2010 Pier 70 Preferred Master Plan and 2012 Blue Greenway Planning and Design Guidelines

    Port of San Francisco, 2018-09-07
  • ~1996MilestoneMission Rock

    Pier 48: Fire destroys Shed C and the eastern third of Sheds A and B

    SF Planning (EIR appendix), 2016-04-11
  • ~1979StatusMission Bay

    Channel Pump Station: Channel Pump Station constructed in 1979 and upgraded in 2010

    SF Planning, Sea Level Rise Vulnerability and Consequences Assessment, ch. 7 Wastewater (2020), section 7.1.1.1 Channel Pump Station, https://sfplanning.s3.amazonaws.com/default/files/plans-and-programs/planning-for-the-city/sea-level-rise/SLRVCA_Report_07.pdf
  • 1965MilestonePotrero Station

    The Stack (Unit 3 smokestack): Unit 3 Power Block and the Boiler Stack constructed (both), extending the Third Street Industrial District's period of significance to 1965 as contributing resources

    SF Planning Department, 2018-10
  • 1965StatusPotrero Station

    The Stack (Unit 3 smokestack): The Boiler Stack (and the adjoining Unit 3 Power Block) are constructed, extending the Third Street Industrial District's period of significance to 1965; the Stack is retained today as an 'Existing Structure' under the Design for Development rather than replaced

    SF Planning Department, 2018-10; SF Planning, 2020-02-26
  • ~1945MilestonePier 70

    Pier 70 Building 21 (Substation No. 5, relocated): Identified on Bethlehem Steel's 1945 plan as Sub-Station No. 5 and Electric Shop No. 2, a government-owned building (owner before 1941: Columbia Steel Co.)

    National Park Service / California Office of Historic Preservation (nomination prepared for the Port of San Francisco by Carey & Co.), 2014-04-17
  • 1941StatusPier 70

    Historic Building 12: Built by U.S. Navy personnel as Plate Shop No. 2, the central building of the New Yard on ground leveled from Irish Hill

    National Park Service / California Office of Historic Preservation (nomination prepared by Carey & Co.), 2014-04-17
  • 1941StatusPier 70

    Pier 70 Building 2 (Warehouse No. 2): Built during World War II as Warehouse No. 2 to support hull construction at the Building 12 complex; sixth floor with drafting room added 1944

    National Park Service / California Office of Historic Preservation (nomination prepared for the Port of San Francisco by Carey & Co.), 2014-04-17
  • ~1941MilestonePier 70

    Pier 70 Building 104 (UIW Headquarters): Building converted to hospital use (the NRHP says the hospital 'most likely' dates from 1941; the building was already called the Navy Office building by 1938), and its rear (north) elevation infilled, giving it its present rectangular footprint

    National Park Service / California Office of Historic Preservation (nomination prepared for the Port of San Francisco by Carey & Co.), 2014-04-17
  • ~1941StatusPier 70

    Pier 70 Building 14: Built as the Heavy Warehouse for equipment used in Machine Shop 1 and ship outfitting (NRHP date; the Port's documents say 1944)

    National Park Service / California Office of Historic Preservation (nomination prepared for the Port of San Francisco by Carey & Co.), 2014-04-17; Port of San Francisco, 2019-01-04
  • ~1938MilestoneMission Rock

    Pier 48: Outer end decked over and connecting Shed C built between Sheds A and B (1937-38)

    SF Planning (EIR appendix), 2016-04-11
  • ~1930StatusMission Rock

    Pier 48: Transit Sheds A and B completed (1929-30) by L.M. King; substructure built 1928-29

    SF Planning (EIR appendix), 2016-04-11
  • Jul 17, 1929MilestoneMission Rock

    Pier 48: Concrete bulkhead wharf completed by Healy-Tibbitts Construction Company

    SF Planning (EIR appendix), 2016-04-11
  • Apr 1926MilestoneMission Rock

    Pier 48: Plans for Pier 48 completed under Chief Engineer Frank G. White of the Board of State Harbor Commissioners

    SF Planning (EIR appendix), 2016-04-11
  • 1917StatusPier 70

    Pier 70 Building 101 (Bethlehem Steel HQ): Built as the Union Iron Works' new main office building to Frederick H. Meyer's design, reported at a cost of $250,000 and 350 staff

    National Park Service / California Office of Historic Preservation (nomination prepared for the Port of San Francisco by Carey & Co.), 2014-04-17
  • Jan 1916MilestonePier 70

    Pier 70 Building 113/114/115/116 (Union Iron Works Machine Shop): Contract of almost $100,000 awarded for the new one-story reinforced concrete foundry (Building 115), under construction by June 1916; Bethlehem's plans date 115/116 to 1917

    National Park Service / California Office of Historic Preservation (nomination prepared for the Port of San Francisco by Carey & Co.), 2014-04-17
  • 1914MilestonePier 70

    Pier 70 Building 113/114/115/116 (Union Iron Works Machine Shop): The two brick buildings joined by a reinforced concrete and steel connector

    National Park Service / California Office of Historic Preservation (nomination prepared for the Port of San Francisco by Carey & Co.), 2014-04-17
  • 1912StatusPier 70

    Pier 70 Building 102 (former Power House): Built as the Union Iron Works powerhouse to Charles Peter Weeks's design; equipment dating from 1913-1914 remained in 2013

    National Park Service / California Office of Historic Preservation (nomination prepared for the Port of San Francisco by Carey & Co.), 2014-04-17
  • ~1901MilestonePotrero Station

    Potrero Power Station Block 15 / Station A: Station A construction begins (completed 1902, with a 1930-31 addition); individually eligible for the California Register under Criterion 1, and a contributor to the Third Street Industrial District

    SF Planning Department, 2018-10
  • ~1901StatusPotrero Station

    Potrero Power Station Block 15 / Station A: Station A's original construction begins (completed 1902, with a 1930-31 addition), predating the Potrero Power Station redevelopment plan by more than a century; the building is retained today (rather than demolished) for adaptive reuse as an office building

    SF Planning Department, 2018-10; SF Planning Department, 2022-03-02
  • ~1900StatusPier 70

    Pier 70 Building 21 (Substation No. 5, relocated): Built circa 1900 as part of the Risdon Iron and Locomotive Works (shown as a machine shop and transformer house on the 1914 and 1936 Sanborn maps)

    National Park Service / California Office of Historic Preservation (nomination prepared for the Port of San Francisco by Carey & Co.), 2014-04-17
  • 1896StatusPier 70

    Pier 70 Building 104 (UIW Headquarters): Built as the Union Iron Works office building, designed by George Percy and Frederick Hamilton

    National Park Service / California Office of Historic Preservation (nomination prepared for the Port of San Francisco by Carey & Co.), 2014-04-17
  • 1885StatusPier 70

    Pier 70 Building 113/114/115/116 (Union Iron Works Machine Shop): Eastern portion of Building 113/114 (blacksmith and boiler shop) completed to civil engineer D. E. Melliss's design; western portion (machine shop) completed 1886

    National Park Service / California Office of Historic Preservation (nomination prepared for the Port of San Francisco by Carey & Co.), 2014-04-17
